significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a linearly decodable evaluation-awareness variable causally modulates refusal, honesty, and compliance, with models showing “larger behavioral eval/deploy gaps” also having “stronger internal evaluation-awareness representations”; this combines a form-(ii) causal claim with a form-(iii) predictive ordering between two measurable quantities. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a shared mechanism across several safety behaviors, constraining explanations of evaluation-conditioned behavior highlighted by the Situational Awareness Dataset (Laine et al., 2024), alignment-faking results (Greenblatt et al., 2024), and in-context scheming evaluations (Meinke et al., 2024). True and false are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out the proposed linearly accessible, causally active shared substrate, although it would not rule out distributed or nonlinear evaluation awareness, so the negative branch is informative but limited. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not earn this score; the score comes from the claim-specific coupling among evaluation context, one internal variable, multiple safety behaviors, and cross-model gap magnitude.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “evaluation-awareness direction,” specifically proposed for “monitoring or ablating this direction during evaluation” to obtain more deployment-representative safety measurements. This is ex ante with respect to accepting benchmark results or shipping a model: an auditor could detect or suppress evaluation-conditioned behavior before relying on the safety score, giving the handle uptake beyond the immediate interpretability research line. Re-extraction would likely be required for each model, but the conclusion predicts a transferable qualitative relation—stronger representations imply larger eval/deploy gaps and steering the direction changes safety behavior—rather than merely supplying an unguided search procedure; the asserted scope is LLMs generally, though architecture and training-regime invariance are unstated. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic safety interpretability supplies no comparable audit-and-ablation handle, whereas this claim specifically gives evaluators and deployment gatekeepers an actionable internal signal.
